layout: 2 panels side by side, each a dense grid of samples with thick black borders (left 7x10 CIFAR-10, right 4x5 CelebA-64 faces)

title: Expert Divergence Learning for MoE-based Language Models
claim: Standard balancing pushes the global expert distribution toward uniform and yields similar experts; ours maximizes divergence between domain-average distributions to produce specialized experts.
layout: 3 panels: (a) MoE layer diagram on left, (b) baseline loss on upper right and (c) ours on lower right, stacked rows with dashed connectors and left-to-right flow in each row

title: Primary-Fine Decoupling for Action Generation in Robotic Imitation
claim: Existing policies collapse modes, jump discontinuously, or bounce between modes on multi-modal demonstrations; ours yields a consistent, fine-grained trajectory.
layout: Left panel of demonstrations, dashed divider, then 4 side-by-side policy panels (a)-(d) left-to-right, each with a failure label on top and the same obstacle circle

title: SeedVR2: One-Step Video Restoration via Diffusion Adversarial Post-Training
claim: Our one-step model matches the quality of slower, larger multi-step baselines while running several times faster, and it restores finer detail than the other baselines.
layout: Large split-view hero image (degraded input left, restored output right) on top; below it a bubble plot of error vs runtime at lower left and a 2-row zoom-in crop grid at lower right, with the input and each method labeled underneath.

title: ChainMPQ: Interleaved Text-Image Reasoning Chains for Mitigating Relation Hallucinations
claim: A baseline model answers a relational query wrongly by hallucinating; guiding it through a chain of decomposed sub-questions with accumulated context yields the correct answer.
layout: 3 regions: input at top-left, method pipeline at top-right, two output boxes at bottom (red failure left, green success right); left-to-right flow with a dashed arrow linking the failure to the image region

title: NextQuill: Causal Preference Modeling for Enhancing LLM Personalization
claim: Aligning models with user preferences should use causal preference effects estimated on both model and data sides, rather than fitting all tokens indiscriminately.
layout: Top row of two boxed pipelines (model-side green, data-side blue) with arrows down into a central alignment box, flanked by two causal graphs at bottom left and right

title: Meta-Adaptive Prompt Distillation for Few-Shot Visual Question Answering
claim: Even with more in-context examples, a model fails to learn the task and keeps producing generic or wrong answers, which motivates a better adaptation approach.
layout: Single left-to-right panel: in-context examples plus query, arrow through an LMM robot icon, then a box of per-shot predictions

title: villa-X: Enhancing Latent Action Modeling in Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: Existing models learn latent actions only from visual reconstruction; adding an auxiliary proprioceptive dynamics module grounds them in physical state and action prediction.
layout: 2 panels split by a dashed vertical line, left-to-right data flow in each, captions (a) and (b) below

title: Learning From the Past with Cascading Eligibility Traces
claim: Standard exponentially decaying traces blur events across a delay, whereas cascaded state-space traces peak sharply at the required delay, giving precise temporal memory.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: A schematic timelines (activity/error, ET vs CET), B family of cascade-state curves, C overlay comparison with legend; dashed line marks target time

title: Deft Scheduling of Dynamic Cloud Workflows with Varying Deadlines via Mixture-of-Experts
claim: A dynamic scheduling environment couples arriving jobs, fluctuating resources and a learned policy in one loop, and we upgrade the policy module with a mixture of experts.
layout: 3 colored panels: (a) left pink workflow environment, (b) top-right blue VM grid, (c) bottom-right orange DRL agent; gray block arrows show state, reward and action loops; dashed arrow from standard policy to MoE policy

title: Variational Autoencoding Discrete Diffusion with Enhanced Dimensional Correlations Modeling
claim: With a single denoising step, the baseline masked diffusion model loses dependencies between dimensions and produces noise, while ours recovers the target structure.
layout: 1x6 row of 2D scatter/density panels, two groups of three (ground truth | baseline | ours), row labels checkerboard and swissroll on the left

title: FutureX: An Advanced Live Benchmark for LLM Agents in Future Prediction
claim: Across many models and agent types, overall scores on a live benchmark stay low, and the strongest systems score only modestly higher than the rest.
layout: single bar chart, models sorted by ascending score left-to-right, color-coded by model category, vendor logos above bars, legend top-left

title: Lavida-O: Elastic Large Masked Diffusion Models for Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
claim: One unified model handles many distinct tasks, including generation, editing, grounding and interleaved reasoning, with high-quality outputs shown for each capability.
layout: 4 dashed rounded panels stacked in a mosaic: wide top gallery, middle row of two panels (editing, grounding), wide bottom reasoning dialogue; colored titles

title: SealQA: Raising the Bar for Reasoning in Search-Augmented Language Models
claim: Scaling test-time compute does not reliably improve accuracy on a hard benchmark; performance often plateaus or declines even as frontier models improve.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots sharing a title, accuracy vs thinking tokens, labeled low/medium/high effort points, legend top-right

title: Translate Policy to Language: Flow Matching Generated Rewards for LLM Explanations
claim: A guidance model supplies positive samples to train a flow-matching reward generator, which yields per-sentence rewards that train an explanation generator via RL.
layout: 3 boxed panels left-to-right (Explanation LLM, Reward Generation by Flow Matching, Guidance LLM), blue arrows linking panels, bar-chart distributions and architecture blocks

title: Explain in Your Own Words: Improving Reasoning via Token-Selective Dual Knowledge Distillation
claim: A weaker or less-confident student shows higher, more erratic token-level uncertainty early in reasoning, so supervising every token overwhelms it and motivates selective distillation.
layout: single line plot, token index on x-axis vs entropy on y-axis, two colored curves with dashed average lines and direct text labels

title: Algorithmic Guarantees for Distilling Supervised and Offline RL Datasets
claim: Our synthetic dataset matches full-data test loss and beats random subsets, with the gap shrinking as synthetic dataset size grows.
layout: 3 panels in a row, each a line plot of test loss vs synthetic size with error bars, shared legend per panel
